subject: AtlasPay - low-latency payments flow: cache seeding + per-route SLA override request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Lowe <michael.lowe@atlaspay.com>, Sara Chen <sara.chen@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AtlasPay - low-latency payments flow: cache seeding + per-route SLA override request

Team — quick context and ask from AtlasPay (pilot customer):

Summary: AtlasPay runs a high-frequency authorization endpoint where they need p50 latency <= 40ms and p95 <= 120ms for a critical fraud-check model used in the authorization path. They are very sensitive to tail latency because every extra 100ms costs them conversion and downstream retries.

What they asked for (customer ask):
- Per-tenant pre-warmed KV cache (keys are small, but warmup needs to be customer-scoped)
- Ability to configure a per-route SLA override (lower batching + tighter latency SLO) for the atlaspay/authorize route
- Pilot target: Nov 15 start; pilot traffic will be 5-10% of production, then ramp if successful

Why this matters: AtlasPay is a strategic enterprise opportunity (deal ATL-3421). They will sign Dedicated capacity if we can hit the pilot SLOs; otherwise they will walk to a competitor. Immediate commercial ask: product/eng decision on feasibility and an ETA for a pilot-safe implementation.

Attachments: AtlasPay_SOW_v2.pdf (commercial), atlaspay_traces_mini.json (sample traces) — I attached the customer-provided traces.

Ask to product/eng: Can we get a feasibility answer and rough implementation plan (ETA, scope, risks) by EOD Monday 10/20? I know this is a heavy ask, but sales needs to finalize commercial terms.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Lowe <michael.lowe@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay - low-latency payments flow: cache seeding + per-route SLA override request

Michael — thanks again for the call this morning. I shared the traces and SOW with our product and eng leads (copied).

Next steps: Grace will follow up with technical clarifying questions; Markus will weigh in on implementation options. We aim to give you a feasibility/approach by Oct 20.

Ben

On a separate note: if you have any additional short traces (10-20 requests) showing cold-cache vs warm-cache behavior that will help our perf analysis.
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Lowe <michael.lowe@atlaspay.com>, Sara Chen <sara.chen@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay - low-latency payments flow: cache seeding + per-route SLA override request

Thanks Ben — quick clarifying questions from product: 

1) Traffic profile: What is the steady-state RPS and the burst RPS during peak (per region)?
2) Key distribution: Are the keys uniform or do you expect a small keyset with very hot keys?
3) SLOs: confirm p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms; do you have p99 target?
4) Rollout constraints: can AtlasPay tolerate short failover to a slightly higher-latency model for 1-2% of requests during incidents?

Engineering note (Markus, feel free to correct): a per-tenant fully-isolated warm cache has memory and operational costs — alternatives include a per-route high-priority lane with prefetch and early-exit logic. We need to pick a design we can pilot quickly and toggle off.

Technical asks for AtlasPay (to evaluate feasibility):
- sample traces (cold vs warm) with ttfb and model latency fields
- expected retention of cached entries (TTL) and key churn rate
- willingness to take reserved capacity or pay a premium for isolation during pilot

If AtlasPay can provide the trace samples and confirm commercial stance on dedicated capacity, we can scope a minimal pilot design (route-level priority lane + pre-seed job + feature toggle) for an initial delivery estimate.

Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Michael Lowe <michael.lowe@atlaspay.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay - low-latency payments flow: cache seeding + per-route SLA override request

Grace / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers below and attaching a lightweight set of traces (atlaspay_traces_mini.json).

Traffic profile: baseline 300 rps per region, peak bursts to ~1.2k rps across regions (we're US-first).
Key distribution: ~2.5k active keys per minute; heavy skew — roughly 200 keys account for ~60% of hits during auth spikes.
SLOs: we want p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms.
Rollout: we can tolerate a tiny fraction (<=1%) of higher-latency fallbacks during the pilot, but long tail failures are not acceptable.
TTL: cached entries are valid for up to 45 seconds; churn is moderate.
Commercial: AtlasPay is prepared to trial Dedicated capacity for the pilot window (short-term commit) and will accept a premium pilot fee if needed. We prefer a toggle-based pilot; if metrics look good we'll finalize the Dedicated contract.

Attached: atlaspay_traces_mini.json (sample traces), perf_trace_samples.zip (aggregated perf logs).

Michael Lowe
Head of Infrastructure, AtlasPay
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Lowe <michael.lowe@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay - low-latency payments flow: cache seeding + per-route SLA override request

Team — technical assessment and proposal: 

Feasibility: OK — we can reach the requested p50/p95 targets with a conservative design that does not require redesigning the serving runtime. Workstream outline: 
- Phase A (pilot-safe): route-priority lane + incremental KV pre-seed job (external-triggered or scheduled) + feature toggle, instrumentation. Expect 3 sprints (6 weeks) to deliver a reliable pilot, assuming a 2-week QA window.
- Phase B (scale/optimize): per-tenant cache isolation improvements, memory accounting, autoscaling knobs. Additional 2-3 sprints.

Risks and tradeoffs: 
- Memory: per-tenant warm caches will increase RAM usage; conservative default is to cap pre-seeded keys per tenant to the top N hot keys (customer-provided heatmap).
- Complexity: priority lanes reduce batching efficiency and increase per-token cost; need to surface cost delta to sales and the customer.
- Measurement: we must instrument end-to-end traces for ttfb and kernel-level latencies during pilot.

Commercial ask for sales: pilot will require either a short Dedicated reservation or a clear pilot premium to offset the cost of lowered batching. If AtlasPay will commit to short Dedicated capacity for the pilot window, we can accelerate Phase A by 2 weeks.

Deliverables for EOD Monday: rough PRD (product) and an implementation estimate (eng). Grace/Ben — I can prepare the eng estimate + risk appendix today if you confirm we should proceed.

—Markus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Lowe <michael.lowe@atlaspay.com>, Sara Chen <sara.chen@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay - low-latency payments flow: cache seeding + per-route SLA override request

All — thanks everyone for the quick responses and the clear assessment. Summary / next steps: 
- Product (Grace): produce one-page PRD for Phase A (route-priority lane + pre-seed + toggle) by COB Mon 10/20.
- Eng (Markus): produce implementation estimate and list of telemetry fields required for pilot by COB Mon 10/20. Markus to include memory/cost delta.
- Sales (Ben/Marissa): confirm commercial pilot (AtlasPay has signaled willingness for short Dedicated reservation). I will draft an amendment to the SOW and include the pilot premium; Marissa will coordinate legal for a 30-day pilot addendum.
- Customer (Michael/Sara): please confirm the attached SOW version is fine and send any additional traces (cold vs warm) you can quickly share.

I'll circle back once Grace and Markus post their artifacts. If we get product/eng greenlight, we will ask AtlasPay to sign the pilot amendment and commit to a start date of Nov 15.

Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
